## webvulns

### Input validation and allowlisting

`security.webvulns.input-validation`: First line of defence for every endpoint: schema-validate structure and type, allowlist values, reject rather than sanitise, and treat redirects/URLs as input too.

- [OWASP Input Validation Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Input_Validation_Cheat_Sheet.html) · CC-BY-SA-4.0 · t1 · reference

### IDOR, BOLA and mass assignment

`security.webvulns.idor-mass-assignment`: Broken object-level authorisation is the number-one API bug; every object fetch needs an ownership/permission check, and binders must allowlist fields.

- [OWASP IDOR Prevention Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Insecure_Direct_Object_Reference_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html) · CC-BY-SA-4.0 · t1 · reference
- [OWASP Mass Assignment Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Mass_Assignment_Cheat_Sheet.html) · CC-BY-SA-4.0 · t1 · reference
- [OWASP API Security Top 10 - API1 BOLA](https://owasp.org/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0x11-t10/) · NOASSERTION · t1 · reference

See also: `security.authz.design`

### Prototype pollution (JavaScript)

`security.webvulns.prototype-pollution`: Merging untrusted objects into JS objects can set __proto__ and reach gadgets in libraries; freeze prototypes, use Map/null-prototype objects, and lint merges.

- [OWASP Prototype Pollution Prevention Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Prototype_Pollution_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html) · CC-BY-SA-4.0 · t1 · reference
- [BlackFan/client-side-prototype-pollution](https://github.com/BlackFan/client-side-prototype-pollution) · none · 1.7k★ · t2 · reference
- [PortSwigger prototype pollution labs](https://portswigger.net/web-security) · none · t2 · reference

See also: `security.lang.nodejs`

### ReDoS and regex safety

`security.webvulns.redos`: Backtracking regexes on user input can hang a service; detect catastrophic patterns and use linear-time engines where possible.

- [makenowjust-labs/recheck](https://github.com/makenowjust-labs/recheck) · MIT · 301★ · t1 · install
- [google/re2](https://github.com/google/re2) · BSD-3-Clause · 9.8k★ · t1 · install

### HTTP request smuggling, race conditions and cache attacks

`security.webvulns.smuggling-race-cache`: Protocol-level bugs between proxies and origins (desync, cache poisoning/deception) and limit-overrun races; mostly fixed by configuration and idempotent design.

- [PortSwigger - HTTP Desync Attacks (request smuggling)](https://portswigger.net/research/http-desync-attacks-request-smuggling-reborn) · none · t1 · reference
- [PortSwigger - Smashing the state machine (race conditions)](https://portswigger.net/research/smashing-the-state-machine) · none · t1 · reference

- [defparam/smuggler](https://github.com/defparam/smuggler) · MIT · 2.1k★ · t3 · reference

### Server-side template injection

`security.webvulns.ssti`: Passing user input into template source (not template variables) gives RCE in Jinja2, Twig, Freemarker and friends; use sandboxed engines and never concatenate templates.

- [PortSwigger SSTI learning path](https://portswigger.net/web-security) · none · t1 · reference

`security.supplychain.dependency-updates`: Keep dependencies current with grouped, tested PRs and a release cooldown so you are neither months behind nor first to install a compromised version.

- [renovatebot/renovate](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate) · AGPL-3.0 · 22.9k★ · t1 · install
- [Renovate minimumReleaseAge docs](https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#minimumreleaseage) · MIT · t1 · reference
- [dependabot/dependabot-core](https://github.com/dependabot/dependabot-core) · MIT · 5.8k★ · t1 · install
- [OWASP Vulnerable Dependency Management Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Vulnerable_Dependency_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html) · CC-BY-SA-4.0 · t2 · reference

See also: `security.supplychain.lockfile-hygiene`, `engineering.ci.dependency-updates-and-pr-automation`

### Lockfile hygiene, install scripts and release cooldowns

`security.supplychain.lockfile-hygiene`: The 2025 npm worm attacks (chalk/debug, Shai-Hulud, nx) spread via install scripts and fresh releases; frozen lockfiles, --ignore-scripts and a minimum release age block most of them.

- [pnpm minimumReleaseAge setting](https://pnpm.io/settings#minimumreleaseage) · MIT · t1 · reference
- [OWASP NPM Security Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/NPM_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html) · CC-BY-SA-4.0 · t1 · reference
- [lirantal/lockfile-lint](https://github.com/lirantal/lockfile-lint) · Apache-2.0 · 870★ · t2 · install
- [lirantal/npq](https://github.com/lirantal/npq) · Apache-2.0 · 1.8k★ · t2 · install
- [OWASP Software Supply Chain Security Cheat Sheet](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Software_Supply_Chain_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html) · CC-BY-SA-4.0 · t1 · reference

See also: `security.supplychain.malicious-packages`, `security.lang.nodejs`

### GitHub Actions and CI pipeline hardening

`security.supplychain.github-actions-hardening`: The tj-actions/changed-files compromise (Mar 2025) showed mutable tags are an attack vector; pin actions by SHA, limit GITHUB_TOKEN, audit workflows for injection.

- [GitHub - Security hardening for GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions) · none · t1 · reference
